01 / 04

An early structured step

I completed Crew Management on Multi-Pilot Aircraft with Alison in January 2024.

Its credential ID is AC-5337-36834668. It was one of my first independent courses and followed my interest in aviation, especially the communication and coordination behind an operation that can look effortless from the outside.

The connection

The course appealed to me because its setting depends on people working towards a shared outcome.

Read the deeper context+

I wanted to understand how they communicate, recognise uncertainty, and keep track of the situation together. Those questions made aviation interesting as a system involving people, not simply a collection of aircraft.

02 / 04

Communication and shared understanding

One useful question to carry from crew management learning is how people build a shared understanding of a situation.

Who has the relevant information? How is uncertainty communicated? What happens when an assumption is left unstated? Those questions make communication more than simply passing on a message.

The connection

I have since noticed related questions in school volunteering and business learning.

Read the deeper context+

When several people contribute to one programme, understanding the immediate task and its purpose matters. The settings are different, but each makes me think about what someone needs to know in order to contribute well.

03 / 04

What I carried forward

Communication is the idea I keep returning to from this course.

Who has the important information? How is an uncertainty raised? What happens when people make different assumptions about the same task? Those are questions I want to practise asking in teamwork, and later in the professional settings I hope to learn about.

The connection

I would like to get better at reviewing a teamwork experience: what made the task clear, what was confusing, and which information helped people move forward.

Read the deeper context+

That gives me something practical to improve. It also makes communication feel like a habit I can work on, rather than a label I attach to myself.
